candidates.exact_span: unless otherwise specified by the permitting authority
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the permitting authority has specified a different turf-harvest restriction changes whether the default 1-year restriction applies, affecting monitoring/compliance expectations and whether applicability remains unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: Turf grown on land where sewage sludge is applied shall not be harvested for 1 year after application of the sewage sludge when the harvested turf is placed on either land with a high potential for public exposure or a lawn
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether harvested turf is placed on high-exposure land or a lawn determines whether the 1-year harvest restriction is triggered, changing which permit-condition obligations are in scope and how missing evidence for those conditions is classified.

candidates.exact_span: Public access to land with a high potential for public exposure shall be restricted for 1 year after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of land as high potential for public exposure determines whether the 1-year access restriction applies versus the 30-day low-exposure rule, affecting which temporal permit obligations are evaluated and unresolved applicability cases.

candidates.exact_span: Public access to land with a low potential for public exposure shall be restricted for 30 days after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of land as low potential for public exposure determines whether the 30-day access restriction applies instead of the 1-year high-exposure rule, changing evaluated permit obligations and missing-evidence handling when site classification is uncertain.

candidates.exact_span: All bulk sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a reclamation site shall be treated by one of the following alternatives 1 through 10 for Vector Attraction Reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge application falls within the listed site types determines whether vector-attraction alternatives 1–10 are mandatory, changing which numeric limits and demonstration/monitoring pathways are applicable.

candidates.exact_span: If bulk sewage sludge is applied to a home garden, or bagged sewage sludge is applied to the land, only alternative 1 through alternative 8 shall be used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Application to a home garden or use of bagged sludge excludes alternatives 9–10 from the compliance set, changing which numeric limits and treatment demonstrations must be evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: The mass of volatile solids in the sewage sludge shall be reduced by a minimum of 38%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 38% minimum volatile-solids reduction is an enforceable numeric threshold whose interpretation (calculation basis, mass accounting) determines whether reported measurements exceed the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an anaerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge anaerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 40 additional days at a temperature between 30 and 37 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 17% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when Alternative 1 'cannot be met,' the bench-test protocol, and the <17% criterion determines which numeric limit applies, whether bench-scale monitoring was required, and how absent primary-path data is classified.

candidates.exact_span: If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an aerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge with a percent solid of 2% or less aerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 30 additional days at 20 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 15% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the aerobic fallback trigger, 2% solids precondition, test duration/temperature, and <15% threshold changes applicable limits, conditional monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence semantics when primary volatile-solids data are absent.

candidates.exact_span: The specific oxygen uptake rate (SOUR) for sewage sludge treated in an aerobic process shall be equal to or less than 1.5 milligrams of oxygen per hour per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) at a temperature of 20 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 1.5 mg O2/hr/g total solids SOUR ceiling is a numeric compliance limit and implies SOUR monitoring at specified conditions; different interpretations of dry-weight basis or temperature correction change limit comparisons and monitoring applicability.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be treated in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer. During that time, the temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 40 degrees Celsius and the average temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 45 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 14-day duration and >40°C / >45°C average temperature thresholds are numeric process conditions; interpretation of treatment duration and temperature measurement/averaging changes compliance determinations and whether temperature monitoring was required.

candidates.exact_span: The pH of sewage sludge shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali shall remain at 12 or higher for two hours and then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The pH 12/11.5 levels and 2-hour/22-hour holding periods are enforceable numeric/temporal limits; interpretation of measurement timing (use/disposal vs bagging) and what counts as additional alkali changes limit applicability and associated monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that does not contain unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 75 % based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 75% solids minimum is a numeric limit whose applicability depends on sludge origin and mixing history; different interpretations of 'prior to mixing' or solids calculation change whether the limit applies and how reported solids measurements are compared.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge contains unstabilized primary-process solids determines whether Alternative 7's 75% solids requirement applies at all, changing applicable numeric limits, monitoring scope, and how missing or ambiguous process-history evidence is resolved.
